facts.fact: Political ad spending reached $10.7 billion in the 2024 election cycle, according to OpenSecrets (2024), a third-party source cited by the page.
facts.quote: Political ad spending hit $10.7 billion in the 2024 election cycle, with a growing share going to streaming and digital channels

facts.fact: According to Kantar's 2024 Media Reactions study (third-party source cited by the page), ad receptivity declines sharply after a consumer sees the same creative more than seven to nine times in a week.
facts.quote: ad receptivity declines sharply after a consumer sees the same creative more than seven to nine times in a week

facts.fact: The page states that in the 2024 cycle, voters in battleground states reported seeing certain political ads 15 to 20 times per week across platforms; no source is given for this figure.
facts.quote: In battleground states, voters reported seeing certain political ads 15 to 20 times per week across platforms.

facts.fact: According to Nielsen (2023), a third-party source cited by the page, optimal frequency for video advertising falls between three and seven exposures per week, depending on campaign goal and creative quality.
facts.quote: optimal frequency for video advertising falls between three and seven exposures per week

facts.fact: The page defines impressions as the total number of times an ad is displayed, so one person seeing an ad five times counts as five impressions.
facts.quote: One person seeing your ad five times counts as five impressions.

facts.fact: The page defines reach as the number of unique individuals or households who see an ad at least once.
facts.quote: the number of unique individuals (or households) who see your ad at least once

facts.fact: The page defines frequency as the average number of times each person in reach sees the ad, and gives an example of 10,000 impressions to 2,000 unique viewers yielding a frequency of 5.
facts.quote: If you serve 10,000 impressions to 2,000 unique viewers, your frequency is 5.

facts.fact: In the Early Awareness Phase (6+ months before the election), the page recommends a frequency cap of 2-3 impressions per household per week.
facts.quote: 2-3 impressions per household per week

facts.fact: In the Persuasion Phase (3-6 months before the election), the page recommends a frequency cap of 4-6 impressions per household per week.
facts.quote: 4-6 impressions per household per week

facts.fact: In the GOTV / Final Push (final 2-4 weeks), the page recommends a frequency cap of 7-10 impressions per household per week.
facts.quote: 7-10 impressions per household per week

facts.fact: The page gives an example CTV/streaming frequency cap of three exposures per week per household, enforced at the household or device level.
facts.quote: You can set a cap (say, three exposures per week per household), and the system enforces it precisely.

facts.fact: The page states that linear TV has no real frequency capping, so an advertiser cannot control how many times one viewer sees a spot.
facts.quote: Linear TV has no real frequency capping.

facts.fact: The page states that digital video cookie-based or login-based frequency caps break down across platforms, so a viewer may hit a cap on one platform yet still see the ad repeatedly on another.
facts.quote: Digital video uses cookie-based or login-based frequency caps, which work reasonably well in a single platform but break down across platforms.

facts.fact: The page states that going above 10 impressions per week per household almost always shows diminishing returns.
facts.quote: Going above 10 impressions per week per household almost always shows diminishing returns.

facts.fact: According to an IAB study cited by the page, political ad recall plateaus after approximately eight exposures per week.
facts.quote: political ad recall plateaus after approximately eight exposures per week

facts.fact: The page's frequency cap table lists a suggested awareness-phase cap of 2-3 per week per household for campaigns 6+ months out.
facts.quote: Awareness | 6+ months out | 2-3/week per household

facts.fact: The page's frequency cap table lists a suggested persuasion-phase cap of 4-6 per week per household for campaigns 3-6 months out.
facts.quote: Persuasion | 3-6 months out | 4-6/week per household

facts.fact: The page's frequency cap table lists a suggested GOTV/final-push cap of 7-10 per week per household for the final 2-4 weeks.
facts.quote: GOTV / Final Push | Final 2-4 weeks | 7-10/week per household

facts.fact: Adwave states its platform lets political campaigns run CTV ads across 100+ premium channels starting at $30 a day.
facts.quote: starting at just $30 a day

facts.fact: According to an IAB source cited by the page, 60% of political media buyers planned to increase CTV spending in 2024 compared to the previous cycle.
facts.quote: 60% of political media buyers planned to increase CTV spending in 2024 compared to the previous cycle

facts.fact: In the page's hypothetical example, a campaign spends $50,000 per week on a target audience of 100,000 households at an average CPM of $25.
facts.quote: your campaign spends $50,000 per week on a target audience of 100,000 households at an average CPM of $25

facts.fact: A 2023 Morning Consult survey cited by the page found that 62% of voters said seeing the same political ad too many times made them less likely to support that candidate.
facts.quote: 62% of voters said seeing the same political ad too many times made them less likely to support that candidate

facts.fact: The page recommends low frequency of 1-2 per week for strong supporters.
facts.quote: Low frequency (1-2 per week). They're already voting for you.

facts.fact: The page recommends moderate frequency of 4-6 per week for persuadable voters.
facts.quote: Moderate frequency (4-6 per week). This is where your budget should concentrate.

facts.fact: The page recommends moderate to high frequency of 5-8 per week for undecided voters.
facts.quote: Moderate to high frequency (5-8 per week).

facts.fact: The page recommends very low frequency of 1-2 per week, or exclusion, for soft opponents.
facts.quote: Very low frequency (1-2 per week) or exclude entirely.

facts.fact: The page flags a red flag when more than 20% of a targeted audience has exceeded the target frequency cap.
facts.quote: more than 20% of your audience has exceeded your target cap

facts.fact: The page's unified cross-channel framework allocates 4-6 CTV impressions per voter per week.
facts.quote: CTV: 4-6 impressions per week

facts.fact: The page's unified cross-channel framework allocates 2-3 digital video impressions per voter per week.
facts.quote: Digital video: 2-3 impressions per week

facts.fact: The page's unified cross-channel framework allocates 3-4 social display impressions per voter per week.
facts.quote: Social display: 3-4 impressions per week

facts.fact: The page's unified cross-channel framework allocates 1-2 direct mail pieces per voter per week.
facts.quote: Direct mail: 1-2 pieces per week

facts.fact: The page states that the combined cross-channel framework totals 10-15 touches per voter per week.
facts.quote: That gives you a total of 10-15 touches per week across all channels

facts.fact: The page advises planning for at least three to four creative variations per campaign phase.
facts.quote: Plan for at least three to four creative variations per campaign phase.

facts.fact: For most political campaigns, the page suggests a frequency cap of four to six impressions per household per week during the persuasion phase.
facts.quote: a frequency cap of four to six impressions per household per week works well during the persuasion phase

facts.fact: The page says that during the final GOTV push, campaigns can increase frequency to seven to ten impressions per week.
facts.quote: During the final GOTV push, you can increase to seven to ten.

facts.fact: The page says early awareness political campaigns should keep frequency around two to three impressions per week.
facts.quote: Early awareness campaigns should stay lower, around two to three per week.

facts.fact: The page recommends comparing engagement, recall, and conversion metrics after two weeks when testing frequency caps of four versus eight on similar audience segments.
facts.quote: If one group gets capped at four and another at eight, compare engagement, recall, and conversion metrics after two weeks.

facts.fact: The page advises increasing frequency in the final two to four weeks before election day, when mobilizing likely voters is the priority.
facts.quote: Increase frequency in the final two to four weeks before election day
